comment: Expected failures caused by the Python SDK (python-sdk, paths relative to src/acp/) or the Python interop programs. Owned by programs/python. See README.md in this directory.

expectations.reason: RFD gap B: the Java client opens the session stream (GET with Acp-Session-Id) before session/load on the new connection; the Python server knows a session stream only once a load or new created it (:196-199), so the GET is a 404 (the legacy interop-python-server XFAIL)

The Java client opens a session-scoped stream for the unknown id "no-such-session" before deleting it; the Python server answers an unknown Acp-Session-Id 404 as the RFD says (http/server.py:300), so delete-unknown-succeeds-silently cannot be observed (as for the Java agent in java.json)

The RFD never lists the session-scoped methods: the Python client sends session/delete without Acp-Session-Id (its list, http/protocol.py:52-58, has no delete) and the Java server requires the header on any request whose params name a session (StreamableHttpRouting defaultRoute), answering 400

The RFD never lists the session-scoped methods: the Python client treats session/fork as minting a session and sends it without Acp-Session-Id (http/protocol.py:52-58), the Java server requires the parent session's header on fork (StreamableHttpRouting, SESSION_FORK rule) and answers 400
The SDK's HTTP server builds each AgentSideConnection without use_unstable_protocol, so session/resume (unstable in the Python SDK) is answered method-not-found although the agent implements it
handle_websocket builds the AgentSideConnection without use_unstable_protocol, so session/resume is answered method-not-found although the agent implements it
The SDK's HTTP server never enables the unstable router: session/close is answered method-not-found
The SDK's WebSocket server never enables the unstable router: session/close is answered method-not-found

The Python SDK has only the $/cancel_request method-name constant: no API to send it

The Python SDK routes no $/cancel_request (only the constant exists), so the #slow handler never sees it and the prompt runs its full 10 s
The Python agent cannot send $/cancel_request (no API), so it answers the chunk "cancel-request unsupported" instead of "cancel-request sent"
The Python agent cannot send $/cancel_request for its pending fs/read_text_file (no API)
create_websocket_stream connects with websockets' default max_size of 1 MiB and offers no way to raise it; a 1 MiB chunk plus its envelope exceeds it and the client closes the socket with 1009
